chapter.title: Works of art, collectors' pieces and antiques

page.h1: HTS Chapter 97: Works of art, collectors' pieces and antiques — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Art & Antiques Exports by Country (HS 97) and Foreign Tariffs | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $10.21B of paintings, sculpture and antiques in 2025. Who buys American art (UK, Switzerland, France, Hong Kong) and what each charges.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$10.21 billion** of works of art, collectors’ pieces and antiques (HS Chapter 97) in 2025, down 1.0% from $10.32 billion in 2024. Paintings, drawings and pastels made entirely by hand (heading 9701) were **72.7%** ($7.42 billion), most of them works less than 100 years old (9701.91, $5.39 billion); original sculpture (9703) added 15.0% and antiques over 100 years (9706) 6.5%. The **United Kingdom** (23.2%) and **Switzerland** (16.2%) were the largest buyers, and the 27 EU countries together took 37.5%, led by France (12.7%). January–August 2026 exports were $7.10 billion, up 2.4%.

Tariffs rarely matter for art. All 12 of the largest buyers charge **0%** on U.S. paintings, prints, sculpture and antiques. The exceptions are **China** (a normal rate of 0–6%, plus 2019 counter-tariffs of 10–25% and the 10% extra on all U.S. goods) and the **UAE** (the 5% Gulf common tariff). What decides access instead are cultural-property and wildlife rules: the EU’s import licence and importer statement for older cultural goods (Regulation (EU) 2019/880, fully applied since June 28, 2025), Swiss customs declarations for cultural property, and ivory and CITES permits on both sides. On the U.S. side, art needs no export licence except to Russia, Belarus and embargoed countries.

keyTakeaways: Hand-made paintings and drawings (9701) are 72.7% of U.S. Chapter 97 exports, original sculpture (9703) 15.0% and antiques (9706) 6.5%; the total was $10.21B in 2025.
The UK (23.2%) and Switzerland (16.2%) bought 39% in 2025, and EU countries together 37.5%; Hong Kong fell 41.9% in 2025 but was up 39.5% in January–August 2026.

Tariffs abroad are almost always zero: the UK, Switzerland, the EU, Hong Kong, South Korea, Japan, Mexico and Canada charge 0% on U.S. art. China is the costly exception, and Canada charged 25% on U.S. original paintings from March 4 to September 1, 2025.

Access turns on paperwork, not duty: the EU’s cultural-goods import licence and importer statement, Swiss cultural-property declarations, and ivory and CITES rules. U.S. art needs no export licence except to Russia, Belarus and embargoed countries.
